title: Kenmu Restoration
capsule: The Kenmu Restoration (建武の中興, 1333–1336) was the short-lived attempt by Emperor Go-Daigo to restore direct imperial rule over Japan after the collapse of the Kamakura Shogunate, which had been overthrown with the help of Ashikaga Takauji and Nitta Yoshisada. Go-Daigo's court at Kyoto sought to govern directly, distributing land and offices without the warrior-class intermediaries that the Kamakura system had relied upon, but rapidly alienated the military aristocracy. Ashikaga Takauji rebelled in 1335–36, drove Go-Daigo from Kyoto, installed a rival emperor, and established the Ashikaga Shogunate, while Go-Daigo fled to Yoshino to establish the rival Southern Court.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Kenmu Restoration controlled most of the Japanese home islands at its outset, but effective authority contracted rapidly from 1335; territorial control is well documented in Japanese chronicle sources (Taiheiki).
